messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xxs and cache-auth errors observed in prod across rate-limiter and auth-cache paths. Affected provider: MemCloud/memcached cluster eu-west. Paging #oncall-sre.

oncall-mary: Acked. I'm seeing a jump in 5xxs starting ~21:11 UTC. Top traces show failures in /auth/validate -> cache lookup failures (ERR auth, connection refused). Pulling logs.

sre-ana: adding context — our serilog shows a flurry of client errors coming from memcloud endpoints: 'CLIENT_ERROR Authentication failed' and 'CONN_RESET by peer'. Also connection counts on sidecar sockets maxing out. Example log:
```
2026-05-18T21:10:59Z ERROR auth-proxy memcache_err="CLIENT_ERROR Authentication failed" host=memcache-eu-12
2026-05-18T21:11:07Z WARN rate-limiter fallback=true reason="conn_reset"
```

eng-tyler: any scheduled maintenance from memcloud side? Or did we push a change to connection pooling earlier today?

account-amy: I see a support banner from MemCloud about a control-plane rolling update in eu-west that started 21:05 UTC. Opened high-priority ticket MC-2026-504.

oncall-mary: impact estimate preliminary: affecting ~1.8% of auth checks, ~0.9% of user-facing requests return 5xx. A few dedicated customers with high QPS report more frequent failures.

support-jess: triaging inbound customer alerts. Notifying top affected accounts with a short message. Will keep comms templated.

eng-tyler: mitigation ideas:
- spin up small in-process LRU token cache for auth-proxy to serve hits when memcached is flaky
- temporarily convert hard 429/403 enforcement in rate-limiter to warn-only for 10m
- increase auth-cache client retry/backoff to reduce storming

sre-ana: agree. I'm toggling the 'soft_fail_on_cache_error' feature flag for auth-proxy and enabling local-lru fallback for auth-proxy instances.

sre-ana: running:
```
rdwctl feature-flag set auth-proxy soft_fail_on_cache_error true --env=prod
rdwctl config apply --service=auth-proxy --env=prod '{"local_lru_enabled": true, "local_lru_capacity": 50000}'
```

ops-bot: Config update initiated by sre-ana @ 21:18 UTC. Rolling.

oncall-mary: also bumping client-side retries for memcache client to 4 with exponential backoff to 250ms base.

eng-tyler: added short-term exception for dedicated customers cust-A47 and cust-B11 to route them to a 'dedicated-auth-fallback' path avoiding the shared cache.

product-ops: flagged priority customers in the incident so account team can follow up post-incident.

memcloud-support-bot: update MC-2026-504 (21:22 UTC): "We've observed a control-plane schema migration causing auth token propagation delays and a temporary throttle on client auth handshakes. Engineering is rolling back the migration for affected nodes. ETA 35-50 minutes." Link: https://support.memcloud/status/MC-2026-504

oncall-mary: good. keeping local fallback and softer rate-limiter rules for now. Monitoring key metrics: auth_cache_error_rate, rate_limiter_5xx, auth_path_latency_p95.

ops-bot: after mitigation (21:26 UTC) metrics: auth_cache_error_rate down from 2.1% -> 0.5%; rate-limiter 5xxs down ~60%. Still seeing occasional spikes on high-QPS tenants.

sre-ana: opened Prod ticket P-5893 and Jira IR-3499. Assigning postmortem owner: sre-ana. Set severity P2. Noting customer impact and actions taken.

support-jess: sent interim notification to affected customers: "We're aware of degraded auth/caching in eu-west from a third-party provider. We have applied local fallbacks and are monitoring. We'll update when upstream confirms rollback." Included suggested mitigations for customers hitting errors.

eng-tyler: pushed a small change to decrease circuit-breaker threshold to avoid thrashing (increase open timeout) and to add jitter on retries to prevent synchronized retries.

sre-ana: reminder — collect heap/memory and connection metrics for auth-proxy pods to ensure local LRU fallback doesn't OOM. Rolling capacity change was conservative.

memcloud-support-bot: update MC-2026-504 (21:45 UTC): "Rollback started for control-plane migration in eu-west. We expect nodes to rejoin and auth tokens to re-sync within 20-30 minutes. We'll post when stabilization observed."

oncall-mary: noting residual risk: dedicated customers routed through high-QPS gateways might still encounter elevated error rates until memcloud nodes fully rejoin.

account-amy: escalating to MemCloud account rep. Requested priority phone bridge.

lauren-night: ack, taking night handoff. I'll monitor alerts and the memcloud ticket. Handoff checklist updated in incident Jira IR-3499.

oncall-mary: handing off to lauren-night at 21:55 UTC. Key watch items:
- sustained auth_cache_error_rate > 0.5% for 10m
- dedicated-customer error reports
- memcloud ticket updates

lauren-night: ack. I have runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/memcache-fallback and credentials for MemCloud rep. Will escalate if anything regresses.

eng-tyler: note for post-incident: evaluate making the local LRU fallback a default safety net for auth-proxy (feature flag on-by-default in high-risk zones). Also add a separate alert for 'memcache_auth_failures' not just generic redis_conn.

sre-ana: agree. Also need to test behaviour for global rate-limiter when cache is degraded — avoid full-blocking policies that cascade.

ops-bot: UPDATE: MemCloud reports stabilization at 22:12 UTC. Nodes rejoined; auth handshakes back to normal. They recommend we keep client-side retry/backoff for 15 minutes to allow residual sync.

lauren-night: verifying metrics (22:20 UTC): auth_cache_error_rate <0.15%, rate-limiter 5xxs at baseline. Removing dedicated-customer exceptions gradually.

support-jess: preparing a follow-up customer message: summary of cause (third-party control-plane migration), mitigation actions (local fallback + soft enforcement), and next steps (postmortem + preventative config changes).

oncall-mary: closing active mitigation. Marking incident as mitigated -> monitoring. Will produce timeline and hand to postmortem owner.

sre-ana: postmortem action items captured:
- get MemCloud RCA and ask for better maintenance windows / notif cadence
- add 'memcache auth failure' alert with paging threshold
- consider default local fallback for auth-proxy in eu regions
- runload test for local LRU behaviour under auth storm
- update runbooks and customer-facing templates

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigated at 22:20 UTC. If errors recur, page oncall.
